resources.string: Private Space: unlock and open apps

"## Enable on a supported device

In Settings → Behaviour, enable the private command and read the compatibility notice. Re:TUI must be the default launcher. Android Private Space support depends on the device implementation; authentication alone does not guarantee that a manufacturer allows another launcher to open private apps.

## Unlock and launch

Run `private -unlock` and authenticate in Android. `private -ls` lists private apps alphabetically. Type an app name at Home to launch an unlocked private app when no personal app matches, or use `private -open <app name>` to explicitly choose the private copy. Replace the placeholder with the full app name. Locked private apps cannot launch; private apps are kept out of general suggestions.

## Lock, hide and settings

`private -lock` locks the space. `private -hide` hides its drawer entry; hiding is not the same as locking. `private -show` restores the entry. `private -settings` asks Android to open the profile settings when supported. If authentication succeeds but apps still do not open, check the device’s own Private Space interface; some manufacturer implementations are incompatible.

## Example

```
private -unlock
private -ls
private -open Example App
private -lock
```"
